sections.h2: How can I sell my house fast in Springettsbury, PA?
sections.html:
Selling to a cash buyer is the fastest way to move a Springettsbury house, with no township sale inspection described on its published pages. Springettsbury Township sits east and northeast of the city of York in York County, and the steps that set the calendar are tax certification, payoff letters and title work.

This page covers what is particular to Springettsbury: its history and neighborhoods, the retail and industrial base around the York Galleria and Interstate 83, the two school districts that split the township, and the tax calendar that determines what the closing company asks you for.

Springettsbury is a supervisor-manager township of about 16.4 square miles, home to the York Galleria mall and a large Harley-Davidson manufacturing campus. The Census Bureau counted 27,058 residents in 2020 and estimates 27,617 for July 1, 2025, a 2.2 percent increase.

The name comes from Springett Penn, a grandson of William Penn, and the township was incorporated on April 20, 1891 out of the northeast part of Spring Garden Township. It includes the census-designated places of East York, Pleasureville, Yorklyn and Stonybrook. East York was first developed in 1903, and the housing built there in the 1930s sits alongside postwar subdivisions such as Fayfield and Haines Acres and newer developments.

Codorus Creek forms the western and northwestern boundary and Mill Creek runs along the southwest. Major roads are Interstate 83, U.S. Route 30, Route 462 (East Market Street), Route 24 and Route 124.

sections.h2: What are the Census numbers for Springettsbury housing?
sections.html:
Census Bureau data for 2020 to 2024 shows 10,202 households, a 72.5 percent owner-occupied rate and a median owner-occupied home value of $243,900. Median gross rent is $1,339, median household income is $86,335 and mean travel time to work is 22.0 minutes.

About 85.8 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, and more than a quarter of homes are rented. Retail sales in 2022 were $1,356,251,000, or $50,118 per resident, which reflects how much shopping in the York area concentrates here.

sections.h2: Which school district is my house in?
sections.html:
Springettsbury is split between the York Suburban and Central York school districts, and your tax bills follow whichever one serves your address. The township tax collector bills school real estate tax for both districts inside the township.

That split matters when you sell. School tax is billed separately from the county and township bill, on a different date, and a closing company needs the right district and the right year to prorate it correctly. Look at your most recent school tax bill, which names the district, before you give a title company the parcel number.

sections.h2: When are Springettsbury tax bills mailed and paid?
sections.html:

The collector goes by postmark date for mailed payments, so allow time. Cash is not accepted in the drop box. If your mortgage company pays through escrow, forward any bill that reaches you rather than paying twice.

sections.h2: How does the tax certification work for a sale?
sections.html:
The closing company asks the township Tax Collector for a Real Estate Tax Certification, which shows whether York County, township, street light and school taxes are paid, with the year, face amount, discount and penalty for each. The request form lists the property address, parcel number, owner, buyer and settlement date and whether the deal is a sale or a refinance.

The fee is $20, payable by check to the Springettsbury Township Tax Collector. Delinquent taxes from prior years go through the York County Tax Claim Bureau instead. The township also keeps a sewer account certification request form among its documents, so ask the title company whether a sewer certification is on its list.

sections.h2: What property rules does the township enforce?
sections.html:
Springettsbury employs a full-time Codes Enforcement Officer who responds to complaints about property maintenance. The township's property maintenance page lists the issues that come up most often:

  • Fences, pools, decks, sheds and patios built too close to a property line.
  • Signs of the wrong size, type or location.
  • Cars, RVs, tractors, construction equipment and boats parked on grass, plus abandoned or junk vehicles.
  • Weeds, tall grass, trash, uncleared sidewalks, dilapidated buildings and unsafe structures.

Owners are asked to correct a violation voluntarily, and a finding can sometimes be appealed to the Zoning Hearing Board. If a violation stays open, the township can pursue legal action and the District Magistrate can impose fines for each violation. Fix open notices before listing, or tell a cash buyer about them up front so the price reflects the work.

sections.h2: What happened to the big employers nearby?
sections.html:
Springettsbury has seen several large facilities change hands. A 101-acre Caterpillar plant operated here from 1953 until the 1990s, and the vacant site was sold in 2002 and redeveloped as the York Business Center. The McCrory Stores headquarters was in the township from 1963 until the chain closed in 2002, and Bon-Ton Stores closed its township headquarters in August 2018.

More recently construction of a Post Consumer Brands logistics center on the Harley-Davidson campus finished in January 2017, and Hollywood Casino York opened in August 2021. For a homeowner, these shifts matter mostly through job access and traffic on Market Street and Route 30.

sections.h2: What about transfer tax and recording?
sections.html:
The state realty transfer tax is 1 percent of value, and local governments can add a share, with the York County Recorder of Deeds collecting it at recording. Certain family transfers and property passed by will or intestate succession are among the exemptions the Department of Revenue lists.

Ask the Recorder of Deeds for the combined local rate for Springettsbury and for current recording fees, then subtract both from your estimate of net proceeds. The sales agreement decides who pays, though both buyer and seller are legally liable if the tax is not paid.

sections.h2: Is a cash sale the right choice in Springettsbury?
sections.html:
A cash sale makes the most sense if the house needs repairs, has an open code violation, is a rental with a tenant leaving, or you need a firm date. Get at least one cash offer in writing, then compare it with the net from a listing after commission, repair credits and the carrying cost of waiting.

Ask any buyer who covers the tax certification fee, the sewer certification and the recording costs, and ask for the closing date in writing.

faqs.q: Does Springettsbury Township require an inspection before I sell?
faqs.a: The township's published pages describe code enforcement for complaints and permits, and they list no sale inspection. Check with the township office about any open violation or permit on your address before listing.

faqs.q: How much is the tax certification in Springettsbury?
faqs.a: The fee is $20, paid by check to the Springettsbury Township Tax Collector. The closing company sends the request form with the parcel number, owner, buyer and settlement date.

faqs.q: Which school districts serve Springettsbury Township?
faqs.a: York Suburban and Central York both serve parts of the township. Their tax bills go out July 1 for York Suburban and July 15 for Central York.

faqs.q: What is the population of Springettsbury Township?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 27,617 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 27,058 in the 2020 census. The township covers about 16.4 square miles.

faqs.q: Where do I pay back taxes on a Springettsbury house?
faqs.a: Delinquent taxes from prior years go to the York County Tax Claim Bureau at 717-771-9232. Current-year bills are paid to the township Tax Collector, who goes by postmark date.
